seo.title: Homeless help in Liverpool - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people who are homeless or at risk in Liverpool: emergency housing, outreach, food, health care, benefits, work and specialist support.

page.heading: Liverpool homeless and housing-crisis help
page.urgent: Immediate danger, serious illness, police, fire or ambulance: 999 or 112 Sleeping outside or nowhere safe tonight: Always Help Available / No Second Night Out 0300 123 2041, 24 hours Council homelessness and emergency housing: 0151 233 3044, day or night Urgent but not life-threatening medical or mental-health help: NHS 111; select the mental-health option for urgent mental-health support
page.notice: Beds, meals, opening times and eligibility can change. Call before travelling when possible. An assessment, outreach contact or referral does not guarantee accommodation. Never pay anyone who claims they can secure a council or charity place.
page.intro:
Tell the worker where you are tonight, where you usually sleep, your age, whether children are with you, and whether pregnancy, disability, illness, domestic abuse, immigration restrictions or a pet affects what is safe. If a service cannot help, ask for the next safe option and write down the advice.
Start here: if you have nowhere safe tonight, call 0300 123 2041. Also contact Liverpool City Council and say clearly that you want to make a homeless application. If you may lose your home within eight weeks, ask for prevention help now.
page.footer: Is something wrong or outdated? Submit a correction. Never post personal or sensitive information publicly. — ../../CONTRIBUTING.md

entries.title: Emergency services
entries.description:
Phone: 999 or 112.
Call for immediate violence, serious injury, overdose, breathing difficulty, loss of consciousness, fire or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark first. If you cannot speak on a mobile call to police, listen and press 55 when prompted.
NHS guidance on calling 999

entries.title: Always Help Available / No Second Night Out
entries.description:
Phone: 0300 123 2041, 24 hours. Call if you are sleeping outside or have nowhere to stay tonight. The Whitechapel Centre operates this service for the council.
Give your location, circumstances and a safe way to make contact. The team can arrange an assessment and connect you with outreach or the temporary Night Assessment Hub when appropriate. The hub has a confidential address and is accessed through the service: it is not a walk-in shelter and a bed is not guaranteed.
Whitechapel urgent help | council rough-sleeper help — https://www.whitechapelcentre.co.uk/get-help.html

entries.title: Liverpool City Council homeless application
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 233 3044, day or night. Use the council's online application as well when you can.
Say clearly that you are homeless or at risk and want to make an application. Explain children, pregnancy, disability, illness, care history, domestic abuse or another reason you may be especially vulnerable. Emergency accommodation depends on the council's legal assessment.
Council homelessness help and application

entries.title: Whitechapel City Region Outreach
entries.description:
Phone: 0300 123 2041. Outreach normally operates Monday–Friday from 7am and at other times when necessary.
Give an exact public sleeping location, time and description. Workers can assess needs and involve health or mental-health nurses. Contact does not guarantee that a person will be found or offered accommodation that day.
City Region Outreach

entries.title: Severe weather
entries.description:
Liverpool makes extra provision during severe weather, including when night temperatures are forecast at 2°C or below and during some storms or high winds. Call 0300 123 2041 and ask whether arrangements are active. Access still requires contact and assessment.
Council severe-weather information

entries.title: Unsafe home or domestic abuse
entries.description:
Call 999 in immediate danger. For housing help call 0151 233 3044. Do not return for papers or belongings if it is unsafe.
National Domestic Abuse Helpline: 0808 2000 247, 24 hours. Men's Advice Line: 0808 801 0327. LGBT+ helpline: 0800 999 5428.
Council housing help if you need to flee

categories.title: Day centres, shelter pathways and housing support

entries.title: Whitechapel Homeless Advice Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 207 7617. Open Monday–Friday 9am–4pm; call first for a same-day appointment.
For people aged 16+ who are homeless or at risk. Housing and welfare advice, prevention, accommodation options, reconnection, and referrals to health and recovery services. People sleeping outside can also ask about showers, laundry and clothing.
Homeless Advice Centre
entries.address: Address: Langsdale Street, Liverpool L3 8DT

entries.title: Hub Homeless Resolution Service
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 207 8677.
- Monday–Friday 8am–3pm: Whitechapel Centre, Langsdale Street, L3 8DT.
- Monday–Friday 3pm–9pm: The Basement, 50–60 Parr Street, L1 4JN.
- Saturday and Sunday 8am–12 noon: Whitechapel Centre.
For new rough sleepers and people at immediate risk, including people staying in squats. You can attend during published hours for assessment. This is not a guaranteed accommodation placement.
Hub and Homeless service leaflet

entries.title: Whitechapel prevention support
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 207 7617; ask for Housing Support, Monday–Friday 12 noon–4pm. An online referral is also available for Liverpool residents.
Ask before an eviction, family breakdown or tenancy problem becomes an emergency. Register with the council's Housing Solutions service as well.
Help when at risk

entries.title: YMCA Together supported accommodation
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 600 3530. Supported accommodation may accept single people aged 16+ after assessment, including people with mental-health, substance-use or offending histories, and some people with dogs.
Access is through the local assessment and referral system. A self-referral starts an assessment; it does not secure a room.
current Homeless England listing
entries.address: Referral address: 15 Leeds Street, Liverpool L3 6HU

entries.title: Night Assessment Hub
entries.description:
This temporary overnight assessment service is reached only through Whitechapel outreach or Always Help Available on 0300 123 2041. Its address is confidential.
Do not travel to an old night-shelter address, and do not assume that making contact guarantees a place.
Whitechapel access information

entries.title: Homeless England directory
entries.description:
Search current accommodation, day centres and specialist services by location and eligibility. Confirm the referral route, vacancies and pet rules directly.
Search Homeless England

entries.title: Whitechapel Centre
entries.description:
People sleeping outside can ask about food and practical essentials alongside showers, laundry, clothing and housing advice. Call 0151 207 7617 first.
Whitechapel Centre
entries.address: Address: Langsdale Street, Liverpool L3 8DT

entries.title: Micah foodbank: St Vincent de Paul
entries.description:
This is a faith-community service, but help is based on need and the parish states that all are welcome.
Micah foodbank access | St Vincent's parish — https://www.stvincentsparish.org.uk/
entries.address: Address: St Vincent de Paul Parish Church, Hardy Street, Liverpool L1 5JN
entries.hours: Open: Tuesday 10:30am–12 noon. Micah offers an emergency three-day food parcel, normally once a week for up to four weeks. The official page says it is open to anybody in need; take bags.

entries.title: Micah foodbank: St Bride's
entries.description: Micah locations
entries.address: Address: St Bride's Church, Percy Street, Liverpool L8 7LT
entries.hours: Open: Thursday 10:30am–12 noon. The same Micah access rules apply. Stock and queues can vary.

entries.title: Liverpool Lighthouse Community Connect
entries.description:
Normally Tuesday–Thursday 10am–3pm in autumn and winter as a warm drop-in with tea, coffee, a pantry and some free hot meals. Published meal times include Tuesday and Wednesday at 12 noon and Thursday at 1pm; pantry Wednesday 12:30pm–2pm.
Wellbeing workers may help with housing, benefits and debt. Confirm the seasonal timetable.
Community Connect
entries.address: Address: Oakfield Road, Anfield, Liverpool L4 0UF

entries.title: Tuebrook Hope Centre
entries.description:
A free community meal is listed for Thursday 12 noon–1pm. Check the current map entry before travelling.
Feeding Liverpool food map
entries.address: Address: Buckingham Road, Tuebrook, Liverpool

entries.title: Columba's Kitchen
entries.description:
Free food support is listed for Friday 9:15am–11:30am. Confirm before a long journey.
Feeding Liverpool listing
entries.address: Address: 76 Pinehurst Road, Liverpool L4 2TZ

entries.title: Hope Community Fridge
entries.description:
Surplus food is normally available Thursday 11am–1pm. Availability depends on donations.
Community food-space map
entries.address: Address: Kensington Elim Church, Coleridge Street, Liverpool L6 6BT

entries.title: Team Oasis Free Food Lounge
entries.description:
Listed sessions include Wednesday 10am–12 noon and some alternate Thursdays 11am–1pm. Confirm whether the Thursday session runs that week.
Feeding Liverpool listing
entries.address: Address: 121–125 Park Hill Road, Liverpool

entries.title: Places of Welcome Community Café
entries.description:
A free community café is listed for Tuesday 12 noon–2pm. Check the map before travelling.
Feeding Liverpool map
entries.address: Address: Christ Church Cabin, 40 Sedgemoor Road, Liverpool L11 3BR

entries.title: Liverpool foodbanks and voucher help
entries.description:
Trussell foodbanks normally require a voucher from a health visitor, social worker, Citizens Advice or another partner. They aim to provide at least three days of emergency food. Church and community services may use different rules.
Call Citizens Advice on 0808 278 7840 if you need referral help.
Council foodbank guidance | Feeding Liverpool crisis support — https://www.feedingliverpool.org/crisis-support/

entries.title: Whitechapel showers and laundry
entries.description:
People sleeping outside can ask for a hot shower, laundry, clothing and practical essentials at Langsdale Street. Call 0151 207 7617 and ask about that day's access.
Whitechapel facilities

entries.title: Asylum Link clothing and essentials
entries.description:
People seeking asylum can ask about essential clothing, meals and practical support Monday–Thursday 9:30am–4pm. Call 0151 709 1713 first.
Asylum Link
entries.address: Address: St Anne's Centre, Overbury Street, Liverpool L7 3HJ; enter through the church car park on Harbord Street

entries.title: Crisis and Resilience Fund
entries.description:
The council may help an eligible Liverpool resident in a sudden financial crisis with clothing and hygiene items. Call 0800 456 1523 or 0151 233 3053, Monday–Friday 8am–6pm. Help is assessed, not guaranteed.
Fund information

entries.title: NHS urgent care
entries.description:
Emergency: 999. Urgent but not life-threatening: 111 or NHS 111 online. Say if you have no fixed address, phone, transport or safe place to recover.
NHS 111 online

entries.title: Brownlow Health homelessness service
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 285 4578. The multidisciplinary service supports people who are homeless or in hostels, with homeless nurses, alcohol and drug workers, outreach and hospital in-reach.
A weekly Homeless Access Clinic is published for Thursday 12:30pm–2:30pm. Call first to confirm the exact clinic site.
Brownlow service | contact details — https://central.brownlowhealth.nhs.uk/contact-us/
entries.address: Central practice: 26 Argyle Street, Liverpool L1 5DL

entries.title: Register with a GP without an address or ID
entries.description:
You do not need proof of address, immigration status, identification or an NHS number to register with a GP. You can use a temporary address or the surgery's address with permission.
Official GP registration rules

entries.title: Urgent dental care
entries.description:
Call NHS 111 for severe pain, swelling, bleeding, infection or a broken tooth when you cannot get a dentist. Call 999 for swelling affecting breathing or swallowing or a major facial injury.
Find an NHS dentist

entries.title: Sexual health services
entries.description:
Use the NHS finder for free, confidential STI testing, contraception and clinics. Ask NHS 111 about urgent symptoms or emergency contraception if a clinic is closed.
Find a sexual-health clinic

entries.title: Urgent mental-health support
entries.description:
Call NHS 111 and select the mental-health option for 24-hour urgent support in Liverpool. Call 999 if there is immediate danger to life.
Samaritans: 116 123, free, 24 hours, for confidential listening.
Mersey Care urgent help

entries.title: River Liverpool drug and alcohol support
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 706 7888. Free, confidential support for adults aged 18+, including assessment, medication, detox or rehabilitation pathways, groups, family support and employment or health help.
Self-refer online or walk into a River hub without an appointment. Published general hours are Monday–Friday 9am–5pm, with Wednesday to 7pm; check the hub first.
River Liverpool

entries.title: Life Rooms
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 478 6556, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. Adults aged 18+ can self-refer for practical wellbeing support concerning housing, benefits, debt, employment, learning and social connection.
Life Rooms is not a crisis service. Use NHS 111 when help is urgent.
Mersey Care help

entries.title: Liverpool Talking Therapies
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 228 2300. Ask about self-referral for non-urgent anxiety, depression and related problems. Waiting times and eligibility vary.
Non-urgent support

categories.title: Toilets, internet, charging and warm spaces

entries.title: Liverpool Central Library
entries.description:
Gender-neutral, accessible and Changing Places toilets are available. Printing costs money. Ask staff before charging a device.
Library facilities | computer rules — https://liverpool.gov.uk/libraries/other-resources/computer-use-in-liverpool-libraries/
entries.address: Address: William Brown Street, Liverpool L3 8EW
entries.hours: Open: Monday–Friday 9am–8pm and Saturday 9am–5pm; closed bank holidays. Free unlimited Wi-Fi does not require membership. Computers require free membership and are walk-up, subject to capacity.

entries.title: Liverpool ONE free toilets
entries.description:
Free toilets include accessible, stoma-friendly and changing facilities. Published hours are Monday–Friday 9am–8pm, Saturday 9am–7pm and Sunday 10:30am–5pm, with different bank-holiday hours.
Liverpool ONE toilets
entries.address: Address: Information Centre, 5 Wall Street, Liverpool L1 8JQ

entries.title: Branch libraries
entries.description:
All Liverpool libraries provide free Wi-Fi; computers, printing and photocopying are also available. Allerton, Garston, Norris Green and Speke Parklands can help with online council tasks. Not every branch has a public toilet.
Find a branch and facilities

entries.title: Liverpool Lighthouse warm space
entries.description:
Community Connect normally provides a warm indoor space, tea and coffee at Oakfield Road, L4 0UF, Tuesday–Thursday 10am–3pm during autumn and winter. Check the seasonal timetable.
Community Connect

categories.title: Transport and Liverpool John Lennon Airport

entries.title: Merseytravel journey planning
entries.description:
Use the official planner and live updates for buses, trains and ferries. Ask a housing, health, council or Jobcentre worker before an appointment whether travel can be authorised; help is not automatic.
Timetables and planner | live disruptions — https://www.merseytravel.gov.uk/travel-updates/

entries.title: City-centre travel help
entries.description:
Liverpool ONE Travel Centre: 1 Canning Place, L1 8LB, Monday–Saturday 10am–5pm. Queen Square: Queen Square Bus Station, L1 1RG, Monday–Saturday 8am–6:30pm and Sunday 10am–5pm.
Ask about routes, fares and tickets. Holiday hours can differ.
Merseytravel Centres

entries.title: Emergency travel costs
entries.description:
The Crisis and Resilience Fund may help an eligible resident with necessary bus fares during a sudden financial crisis. Apply before buying a ticket when possible.
Crisis and Resilience Fund

entries.title: Liverpool John Lennon Airport by bus
entries.description:
The 500 links Liverpool ONE and the airport about every 30 minutes; Arriva publishes a journey of about 30 minutes and service from around 4am to midnight. Routes 80A and 86A also connect the city, Liverpool South Parkway and airport.
Check the day's timetable and fare. The terminal is not accommodation; if stranded with nowhere safe, call 0300 123 2041.
Current airport bus routes

entries.title: Airport connection by train
entries.description:
Liverpool South Parkway is the nearest main rail station. Continue by an 80A, 86A or other current airport bus. Some rail tickets can include the bus connection when the destination is Liverpool John Lennon Airport.
Rail and bus connection

entries.title: Liverpool Crisis and Resilience Fund
entries.description:
Phone: 0800 456 1523 or 0151 233 3053, Monday–Friday 8am–6pm.
Liverpool residents aged 16+ on a low income may receive short-term help after a sudden financial crisis. Possible help includes food, utilities, clothing, hygiene, furniture, travel, phone or internet and some rent shortfalls or housing costs. You do not have to receive benefits.
An award is not guaranteed. Urgent cases may be decided within 48 hours. Apply online, by phone, through a One Stop Shop or support organisation.
Fund rules and application

entries.title: Universal Credit without a fixed address
entries.description:
You can claim while rough sleeping, sofa surfing or staying in a hostel. With permission, use a trusted person's, hostel, day-centre or Jobcentre address. If you lack ID, a bank account, phone, email or National Insurance number, say so: alternatives may be possible.
Tell your work coach about homelessness, mental ill health or recovery needs and ask whether your claimant commitment should change temporarily.
Universal Credit guidance

entries.title: Citizens Advice Liverpool
entries.description:
General advice: 0808 278 7840, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. Free advice on benefits, housing, work, family, immigration, consumer problems and discrimination.
Debt: 0300 330 1196, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. High-demand drop-ins may close when full.
Citizens Advice | debt help — https://citizensadviceliverpool.org.uk/debt-money/

entries.title: Council benefits advice and appointments
entries.description:
The council can check entitlement, help with forms and challenges, and refer urgent problems. For a face-to-face or phone benefits appointment call 0151 233 3009, Monday–Friday 8am–6pm.
Appointments use selected branch libraries. Say if you have no internet, phone, ID or safe correspondence address.
Benefits advice | One Stop Shops — https://liverpool.gov.uk/customerhubs

entries.title: Housing Benefit in supported accommodation
entries.description:
Housing Benefit can still apply to some hostel, supported, sheltered or council-arranged temporary accommodation even when other costs use Universal Credit. Ask the provider and council which claim is correct.
Housing Benefit guidance

categories.title: Work, training and travel to a new job

entries.title: Liverpool in Work
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 233 5312; email: liverpoolinwork@liverpool.gov.uk. — mailto:liverpoolinwork@liverpool.gov.uk
Free personalised employment help for Liverpool residents aged 18+, including skills, confidence, apprenticeships, work trials and one-to-one support. Connect to Work is for jobseekers facing additional barriers.
Liverpool in Work

entries.title: Find vacancies and a Jobcentre
entries.description:
Use the official Find a Job service and postcode search for a current Jobcentre. Do not rely on an old office address. A Jobcentre can help with Universal Credit, work-coach appointments and National Insurance questions.
Find a Job | find a Jobcentre — https://find-your-nearest-jobcentre.dwp.gov.uk/

entries.title: National Careers Service
entries.description:
Free advice on CVs, interviews, qualifications, training and careers for adults in England. Ask for phone or online support if you cannot travel.
National Careers Service

entries.title: Life Rooms employment and learning help
entries.description:
Call 0151 478 6556 for practical help with employment, learning, benefits and housing when wellbeing or mental health is also a barrier. It is not a recruitment agency or emergency service.
Life Rooms

entries.title: Travel, phone or essentials for work
entries.description:
The Crisis and Resilience Fund may help an eligible resident with travel, phone or internet costs during a sudden crisis. A Jobcentre work coach may consider the Flexible Support Fund for agreed work costs. Ask before paying; neither is automatic.
Liverpool crisis support

categories.title: Housing law, debt and legal advice

entries.title: Shelter Merseyside
entries.description:
New Legal Aid appointments: 0344 515 1300, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm. Appointment and eligibility check required.
National emergency housing helpline: 0808 800 4444, Monday–Friday 8am–5pm.
Shelter Merseyside
entries.address: Legal Aid service: Holy Trinity Church, Richmond Park, Liverpool L6 5AD

entries.title: Merseyside Law Centre
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 709 0504. Free specialist housing advice and representation for Merseyside residents who cannot afford it; welfare-benefit advice is currently limited to Liverpool City Council residents.
Drop-in clinics are wheelchair accessible. Check the current timetable and funding criteria.
Merseyside Law Centre
entries.address: Address: Kuumba Imani Millennium Centre, 4 Princes Road, Liverpool L8 1TH

entries.title: Citizens Advice Liverpool
entries.description:
Call 0808 278 7840, Monday–Friday 9am–5pm, for free advice on housing, benefits, work, family and some immigration issues. For debt call 0300 330 1196.
Take notices, court papers, tenancy papers and benefit letters if you have them, but seek help even when papers are missing.
Citizens Advice Liverpool

entries.title: Civil Legal Advice
entries.description:
Call 0345 345 4345. Legal Aid advice may be available for eligible housing, debt, discrimination and domestic-abuse problems.
Do not miss a court hearing while waiting for advice. Take the papers and ask about the Housing Possession Court Duty Scheme.
Civil Legal Advice

entries.title: National Insurance number
entries.description:
Check old payslips, benefit letters, a tax account or UKVI account first. You may start work before receiving a number if you can prove the right to work, and do not need one to start a benefit claim.
Apply for or find a number

entries.title: Prove the right to work
entries.description:
British and Irish citizens may use an eligible passport or a birth or adoption certificate together with an official document showing their National Insurance number. Other people may use a share code or eligible immigration documents.
Do not pay an unofficial agent. Ask Citizens Advice or a regulated adviser if status is unclear.
Official right-to-work service

entries.title: Replace a birth certificate
entries.description:
Order through the General Register Office or relevant register office. Fees apply. Ask a support worker about safe delivery and possible fee help.
Order a certificate

entries.title: Passport advice
entries.description:
Contact HM Passport Office before paying if documents, referees or delivery are difficult. A charity may help you apply but cannot guarantee the fee.
Passport Adviceline

entries.title: Phone and online access
entries.description:
Libraries provide free Wi-Fi, and Central Library has walk-up computers for members. The Crisis and Resilience Fund may assess phone or internet costs; equipment or credit is not guaranteed.
Library internet | crisis fund — https://liverpool.gov.uk/crf

entries.title: Mail and document storage
entries.description:
Ask whether a hostel, day centre, trusted person or Jobcentre can authorise a care-of address. Confirm collection rules.
Do not send post or leave identification, papers or belongings at a service without explicit permission. No verified open-access public luggage-storage service was found.
Care-of address options

entries.title: Asylum Link Merseyside
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 709 1713. Open Monday–Thursday 9:30am–4pm.
Casework, immigration advice within its authorisation, English classes, wellbeing activities, hot meals, clothing and help accessing housing, GPs and services. Priority is given to people in Liverpool City Region and areas with little specialist support.
Asylum Link
entries.address: Address: St Anne's Centre, Overbury Street, Liverpool L7 3HJ; enter through the church car park on Harbord Street

entries.title: Migrant Help asylum helpline
entries.description:
Freephone: 0808 8010 503. Help with asylum support, destitution, accommodation problems and finding legal representation. Migrant Help is not a law firm.
GOV.UK asylum helplines

entries.title: Refugee Women Connect
entries.description:
Support for women asylum seekers, refugees and survivors of trafficking across Merseyside, including outreach, weekly drop-ins, emotional and practical support, English learning and access to services.
Locations can change. Contact the team before attending.
Refugee Women Connect

entries.title: Sahir: LGBTQ+ refugees and asylum seekers
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 673 1972, weekdays 10am–4pm; email: info@sahir.org.uk. — mailto:info@sahir.org.uk
Information, advice and signposting, plus counselling, HIV and wider LGBTQ+ health and wellbeing support.
Sahir services

entries.title: Modern Slavery and Exploitation Helpline
entries.description:
Call 08000 121 700. Current temporary hours are 12 noon–5pm daily. Call 999 for immediate danger.
Confidential guidance if someone is controlled, threatened, forced to work or have sex, has pay or documents withheld, or cannot leave.
Modern Slavery Helpline

entries.title: Liverpool Domestic Abuse Service
entries.description:
Freephone: 0800 084 2744; office: 0151 263 7474. Open Monday–Thursday 9am–5pm and Friday 9am–3pm.
Women-led, women-only support for women and girls affected by domestic abuse, including drop-in, referral and outreach. Refuge depends on assessment and availability.
LDAS contact

entries.title: Domestic-abuse help for all survivors
entries.description:
The council lists local services for women, men, families and young people. Merseyside Domestic Violence Service: 07802 722703. Paul Lavelle Foundation for men: 0151 651 3777.
Call 999 in immediate danger. Ask for an interpreter if needed.
Council domestic-abuse services

entries.title: Young people and YMCA Together
entries.description:
People aged 16+ may be assessed for supported accommodation. Call Always Help Available on 0300 123 2041 or YMCA Together on 0151 600 3530.
If under 18, say your age immediately and ask for Children's Services. Call 999 if in danger. Sofa surfing still counts as homelessness.
YMCA Together listing

entries.title: Care leavers
entries.description:
Liverpool must help if you were looked after by any local authority while aged 16 or 17. Care leavers aged 21–25 can also ask the leaving-care service for homelessness help.
Tell Housing Options that you are a care leaver and contact your personal adviser.
Care-leaver housing help

entries.title: Sahir: LGBTQ+ and HIV support
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 673 1972, weekdays 10am–4pm. LGBTQ+ health and wellbeing, counselling, peer groups, advocacy, HIV support and help for LGBTQ+ refugees.
Sahir is not emergency accommodation. For domestic-abuse support call Galop on 0800 999 5428.
Sahir Liverpool
entries.address: Address: 2nd Floor, 151 Dale Street, Liverpool L2 2AH

entries.title: Liverpool Veterans HQ
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 261 9878; email: info@veteranshqliverpool.com. — mailto:info@veteranshqliverpool.com
In-person support concerning housing, health, addiction, welfare, debt, legal issues, work, training and social connection. Contact does not guarantee accommodation.
GOV.UK listing
entries.address: Address: 28 St Domingo Vale, Liverpool L5 6RW

entries.title: Op FORTITUDE: veterans at risk
entries.description:
Call 0800 952 0774. Veterans can self-refer for housing and tenancy support through the national pathway. Accommodation is individually assessed.
Op FORTITUDE

entries.title: Age Concern Liverpool and Sefton: age 50+
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 330 5678, Monday–Friday 10am–3pm.
Free information and signposting on benefits, debt, housing, health, social care and local services.
Age Concern information
entries.address: Address: The Frances Suite, 1st Floor, 151 Dale Street, Liverpool L2 2JH

entries.title: Adult social care, disability and safeguarding
entries.description:
Phone: 0151 459 2606. Call if illness, disability, injury, abuse, neglect or self-neglect affects an adult's daily living or safety. Call 999 for immediate danger.
Social care does not replace a homeless application. Contact both services if care needs affect safe accommodation.
Adult social care | report abuse or neglect — https://liverpool.gov.uk/publicsafeguarding

entries.title: StreetVet Liverpool
entries.description:
Volunteer vets provide a monthly city-centre outreach clinic for pets belonging to people experiencing homelessness. Care can include checks, vaccinations, microchipping, parasite treatment, medication and pet essentials.
The public date and location are not fixed on the official page. Use the help form or ask Whitechapel. StreetVet is not an emergency service.
StreetVet Liverpool | request help — https://www.streetvet.org.uk/get-help-now/

entries.title: Dogs Trust Together Through Homelessness
entries.description:
The UK-wide scheme helps eligible dog owners with veterinary costs and finding dog-friendly services. A participating homelessness service may need to apply. Assessment applies; existing bills and every procedure are not automatically covered.
Together Through Homelessness

entries.title: Tell every service about your pet
entries.description:
Some placements accept pets and others do not. Tell the council and referrer the species, size, health, behaviour and vaccination status. Ask for a pet-friendly option before accepting or rejecting a placement.
Do not abandon an animal or arrive at an unknown hostel expecting admission.
Search dog-friendly services
